max_check_bytes.description: The largest text, in UTF-8 bytes, the hook parses (1 MiB, so a parse stays well inside `external_timeout_ms`). A larger one is not parsed at all and answers `none` with its language and the note `too_large_to_check`, so no parser can hang on it.

description.purpose: The syntax hook of a file space (GH #901): judges a new text version before `./write` lets it land. JSON, TOML and Python are parsed with the Python standard library (`json`, `tomllib`, `ast` -- nothing is executed); every other kind of file has no hook. One register, `HOOKS`, names every language with its endings, MIME types and checker; a registered MIME type wins over the ending, and the ending is compared without case.
description.use_when: Reached on `in_check` only, which `./write` draws for every text version of a write without `force`; answered on `checked` with the asker's `op_id`, which `./write` draws back to itself.
description.not_in_scope: No refusal of its own and no store: `./write` turns `failed` into its `syntax` refusal and records `force` on the version. No state, no environment, no network, no file; the same request gets the same answer. Markdown, plain text and source languages without a standard-library parser (Rust and the like) have no hook here.
description.emits_meaning: hook: `ok` (parsed), `failed` (the parser refused), `none` (nothing was checked: binary, no hook for the file, or see `note`). lang: the language the register resolved, '' when none applies. error {message, line, col}: on `failed`, the parser's message and the place it stopped, both 1-based as the parser reports them (0 = not named). note: `too_large_to_check` over `max_check_bytes`, `too_deep_to_check` when the nesting exceeds the interpreter's stack, `no_text` when a text version came without `text`.
description.consumes_meaning: body.path: the file's path in the space (its ending picks the language when the MIME type does not). body.mime: the file's MIME type, parameters ignored. body.kind: only `text` is checked; `binary` answers `none`. body.text: the whole new content.
examples: {"path":"conf/app.json","kind":"text","text":"{\"a\":1,}"} -> {"hook":"failed","lang":"json","error":{"message":"Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes","line":1,"col":8}}
